title: Chicago Cubs and Cardano: Transforming team operations with innovative technology to enhance performance and fan engagement in sports.

ms.promise:
1. Needs Assessment: Identifying club’s specific blockchain needs and opportunities with Cardano

2. A comprehensive Cardano-centric syllabus for a five-part workshop series (up to 2 hours each session) covering:
 - Session 1: Introduction to Blockchain and Cardano Ecosystem 
 - Session 2: Blockchain & Web3 in Sports 
 - Session 3: Fan Engagement on Cardano 
 - Session 4: Enhanced Security and Data Integrity with Cardano 
 - Session 5: Exploring Cardano DApps for Sports Applications

3. Tailored educational materials:
 - Slide decks (PowerPoint or PDF) tailored to each topic
 - One case study of blockchain in sports per session above (5 in total)
 - PDF (one page) summary for participants after each session. 
 - A glossary of blockchain and Cardano terminology for the teams leadership 

4. A comprehensive analysis of 10 Cardano DApps, including: 
 - Name, purpose, and relevance to the sports industry. 
 - Use case examples tailored to Chicago Cubs’s operations and needs 
 - A short presentation for at least 3 DApps showcasing their potential application.

We endeavour to explore many more DApps within the Cardano ecosystem where we see a clear fit for sports.
ms.criteria:
- Needs Assessment approved by eitherChicago Cubs Director of Baseball Innovation - Bobby Basham or Vice President of Technology - Steven Inman
- Syllabus approved by either Chicago Cubs Director of Baseball Innovation - Bobby Basham or Vice President of Technology - Steven Inman
- Educational materials reviewed and accepted by Cardano Foundation (Pierre Kaklamanos)
- DApp analysis validated by at least one blockchain consultant specializing in sports (Ben Illian, Book.io)

Dear reviewer;
ADDRESSING OUR COMMENTS:
Thanks for your notes, please see our response below;
The needs assessment was never defined or planned as anything other than a fact finding exercise for us with the club. We are the ones with the expertise and experience of dealing with the teams and clubs at this high level. The fact-finding has come up in multiple phone conversations with the Cubs so far. This, in our opinion, forms part of Session 1 in Milestone 2. This is the way we have planned it & it has worked very well for them in the first session. The feedback/summary of the Sessions will be uploaded as POA at the end of Milestone 2 - not at this stage in Milestone 1 - this will showcase the Cubs understanding & their "needs".
As it relates to your other notes - We will continue to work on the organization of the materials to be easily understood - folders are now more clearly defined.
